newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CDL Hotels shares rise on merger report.
newsitem.headline: CDL Hotels shares rise on merger report.

text.p: Shares in CDL Hotels International Ltd rose on Tuesday on a newspaper reports that the hotelier planned to merge with a luxury hotel chain to raise its international profile, brokers said on Tuesday.
Its shares rose HK$0.10 or 2.45 percent to an intraday high of HK$4.175 in early afternoon on volume of 1.22 million shares.
"Anticipation its asset base will be enlarged by the possible merger fueled buying," said a local research manager.

Local press reported CDL's parent Hong Leong group aimed to merge CDL with an international hotel chain. Potential suitors were likely to include Regent, Fairmont and Hilton hotel groups, the reports.
The company's officials were not available for comment.
CDL, which has hotel interests in Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia and the Philippines, was 57.8 percent held by Hong Leong as in July.
